rows.proof: THE TRUST FUND STATEMENT'S OWN `GRAND TOTALS`, printed on PDF page 38 (`Page 2 of 3`) of the FY2017 annual town report, against the SIX group `SUBTOTALS` lines the statement prints -- three on page 37 (CEMETERY, CONSERVATION, LIBRARY) and three on page 38 (SCHOLARSHIP, MISCELLANEOUS, STABILIZATION). ALL NINE COLUMNS CLOSE TO THE CENT: $2,273,700.80 / $187,191.63 / $112,634.17 / $31,649.20 / ($19,335.24) / ($18,314.75) / $2,567,525.81 / ($23,347.80) / $2,608,445.39. THIS IS THE GRAIN OF SUBTOTALS, NOT OF FUNDS, and it must never be added to `fy2017-p37-trust-cemetery.csv` and its siblings, which hold the funds beneath these same subtotals. It exists because the two columns no row identity on page 37 touches -- `UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS` and `ENDING MARKET VALUE` -- are otherwise checked only by their own group subtotal, and this is a second, independent printing of the same quantity. HOW IT WAS READ: pages 37 and 38 are single embedded scans and were read off their own bitmaps with pypdf at native resolution (230 dpi), rotated upright. No recognition, neither renderer. *** AND IT IS WHERE THE ARCHIVE'S KNOWN -$19.00 COMES FROM, WHICH IS OURS AND NOT THE TOWN'S. *** `notes/HANDOFF-ANNUAL-REPORTS.md` records that FY2017 trust funds `read their own grand totals as -$19.00`. That row is in `report-trust-funds.csv`, on PAGE 38, labelled `GRAND TOTALS`, kind `grand_total`, and it carries ONE value -- `v2 = -19.00` -- with the other eight columns EMPTY, against a printed row that holds NINE complete figures. The page cache is not the problem and was checked: `report_pages.load('FY2017')[38]` holds the line in full, `$2,273,700.80 $187,191.63 $112,634.17 $31,649.20 ($19,335.24) ($18,314.75) $2,567,525.81 ($23,347.80) $2,608,445.39`. So the defect is in the generic extractor's COLUMN RULER for this page, not in the document and not in the reading of it. A HYPOTHESIS THAT FITS AND IS NOT TESTED HERE: -19.00 is the left-hand fragment of `($19,335.24)` cut at its thousands comma, which is the ruler-splits-a-figure defect this project has recorded before. -$19.00 is NOT a figure the town prints anywhere; no fund is nineteen dollars overdrawn.

rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / TRUST FUNDS / FISCAL YEAR 2017 SUMMARY`, `Page 1 of 3`, PDF page 37 of the FY2017 annual town report. THE PRINTED HEADER, VERBATIM, COLUMN BY COLUMN: `ACCOUNT NUMBER` | `FUND NAME` | `FY 2017 BEGINNING PRINCIPAL` | `FY 2017 BEGINNING EARNINGS` | `FY 2017 CONTRIBUTE TO PRINCIPAL` | `FY 2017 NET EARNINGS` | `FY 2017 DISBURSE FROM PRINCIPAL` | `FY 2017 TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS` | `FY 2017 ENDING CASH VALUE` | `FY 2017 UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS` | `FY 2017 ENDING MARKET VALUE`. Every column heading was READ off the page and written down; none is inferred. THE `ACCOUNT NUMBER` COLUMN IS PRINTED AND EMPTY on every row of this page. WHAT THE PAGE HOLDS, counted off the page rather than off any dataset: THREE groups and TWENTY-TWO funds -- `CEMETERY FUNDS` (3), `CONSERVATION FUNDS` (5), `LIBRARY FUNDS` (14) -- each group closed by its own `SUBTOTALS` line. It is page 1 of 3; the scholarship, miscellaneous and stabilization groups and the statement's `GRAND TOTALS` are on page 38. HOW IT WAS READ: the page is a SINGLE EMBEDDED SCAN -- pdfplumber returns one word (the folio) and one image -- so the scanner's own pixels were taken straight off the PDF with pypdf, rotated upright and cropped into two column blocks, each with the fund-name strip pasted beside it so a figure stays attached to the row it is printed on. Neither render script was used, so neither could clip it. WHAT PROVES IT, three ways, AND EVERY ONE CLOSES TO THE CENT WITH NO TOLERANCE AT ALL. (1) TWENTY-TWO ROW IDENTITIES: beginning principal + beginning earnings + contribute to principal + net earnings + disburse from principal + transfers of earnings = `ENDING CASH VALUE`, on all 22 funds, exactly. (2) TWENTY-SEVEN COLUMN SUBTOTALS: nine columns against each of the three printed `SUBTOTALS` lines, all 27 exactly. (3) THE STATEMENT'S OWN `GRAND TOTALS`, WHICH ARE PRINTED ON PAGE 38 AND FOOT ACROSS BOTH PAGES: this page's three subtotals plus page 38's three add to all nine printed grand totals to the cent -- $2,273,700.80 / $187,191.63 / $112,634.17 / $31,649.20 / ($19,335.24) / ($18,314.75) / $2,567,525.81 / ($23,347.80) / $2,608,445.39. That cross-page reconciliation is `fy2017-p37-trust-grand-totals.csv` and it is what makes the `UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS` and `ENDING MARKET VALUE` columns checkable at all. *** THIS PAGE STATES NO IDENTITY LINKING `UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS` TO `ENDING MARKET VALUE`, AND THE ONE THE ADJACENT YEARS STATE DOES NOT HOLD HERE. *** FY2018 page 44 and FY2021 page 40 both close on `ending cash value + unrealized gain/loss = ending market value`. On this page that identity fails on every row: PERPETUAL CARE BEQUEST is $187,455.81 cash and ($1,847.76) unrealized against an ending market value of $190,443.36, which is $4,835.31 the other way. What the figures DO show is that `ENDING MARKET VALUE` divided by `ENDING CASH VALUE` is 1.015937 on every one of the 22 funds and on all three subtotal lines, and that `UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS` divided by `ENDING CASH VALUE` is -0.009857 on every one -- two constant pro-rata allocations across the whole page. THAT IS A REGULARITY, NOT AN IDENTITY THE PAGE STATES, so it is NOT used as a check here: offering it as one would be a hypothesis dressed as a proof. WHAT THE COLUMN MEANS IS NOT ESTABLISHED -- cumulative unrealized gain, the year's change in it, and a custodian's allocation all fit the same figures -- and nothing on the page says. The two columns are instead proved by their subtotals and by the cross-page grand totals, which is what rule 7b's advice amounts to for a column no row identity touches. ONE FUND NAME IS CLIPPED BY THE DOCUMENT ITSELF. The last library row prints `ANNIE & ARTHUR BILLINGS CULTURAL TR` and the name runs into the `BEGINNING PRINCIPAL` column and is cut off there by the page, not by the reading. It is transcribed as the page prints it; the full name is not recoverable from this page. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. A trust fund balance is not money the town may spend: the purpose, the restriction and the donor's terms are nowhere on this page, and nothing here says which of these funds is expendable. `TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS` and `DISBURSE FROM PRINCIPAL` record that money moved; they do not say where it went or what it bought. And the ACCOUNT NUMBER column being empty means these funds cannot be joined to the general ledger from this page.

rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30, 2017`, PDF pages 41 and 42 of the FY2017 annual town report. ONE TABLE ACROSS TWO PAGES: fifteen debt issues against THIRTY fiscal years, FY2018-FY2028 on page 41 and FY2029-FY2047 on page 42, each issue in three printed rows -- PRINCIPAL, INTEREST and the issue's own TOTAL -- and the two pages carry the identical fifteen issue labels in the identical order. THE PRINTED HEADER, VERBATIM: the left column is headed `FISCAL YEAR`; the money columns are headed only by the year, `2018` to `2028` on page 41 and `2029` to `2047` on page 42. There is no TOTAL column and no per-issue total: this schedule prints its arithmetic DOWN the page, in three rows at the foot of every year column -- `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL`, `GRAND TOTAL INTEREST` and `TOTAL DEBT`. A footnote runs under both pages: `*MASS WATER POLLUTION ABATEMENT TRUST: PAYMENT AMOUNTS TO BE SUBSIDIZED BY EQUITY EARNINGS AND CONTRACT ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS`. HOW IT WAS READ: each page is a SINGLE EMBEDDED SCAN -- pdfplumber returns one word (the folio) and one image -- so the scanner's own pixels were taken straight off the PDF with pypdf, rotated upright and cropped into column blocks with the label strip pasted beside each block, which is how a figure is kept attached to the row it is printed on. No render scale adds detail a scan does not hold, and neither render script was used, so neither could clip the page. THE GRAIN IS ONE FILE PER FISCAL YEAR, which is what makes this page checkable: the schedule's own arithmetic runs down each year column, so a year is the unit the document proves. Each file holds that year's fifteen issues against the three GRAND TOTAL rows the page prints beneath them. Thirty files, THIRTY INDEPENDENT YEARS, ninety column assertions. WHAT PROVES IT, three ways on every year. (1) THE COLUMN: the fifteen issues' PRINCIPAL adds to the printed `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL`, their INTEREST to `GRAND TOTAL INTEREST`, and their issue TOTALS to `TOTAL DEBT`. (2) THE ROW: principal + interest = the issue's own printed TOTAL, on every issue-year the page prints a total for -- 198 of them. (3) The page's two grand totals add to its own `TOTAL DEBT`. ALL NINETY COLUMN ASSERTIONS AND ALL 198 ROW IDENTITIES CLOSE WITHIN ONE DOLLAR, and most close exactly: 2018 principal ties to the dollar at $2,985,086 across fifteen addends and 2029 principal at $1,413,855 across eight. THE DECLARED TOLERANCE IS $1.00 AND IT IS DERIVED, NOT FITTED. The schedule displays WHOLE DOLLARS over amounts that carry cents -- the MWPAT loans and the sewer and water issues all do -- so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts. The widest column on either page has FIFTEEN addends (FY2018), so the arithmetic bound on a column is 15 x $0.50 plus the printed total's own $0.50, i.e. $8. THE OBSERVED MAXIMUM ACROSS ALL 90 COLUMN ASSERTIONS AND ALL 198 ROW IDENTITIES IS $1. The tolerance is set at the observed maximum and sits seven times inside the arithmetic bound. It is NOT a safe guard against a misread of the UNITS digit, because these are whole-dollar displays and such a misread also costs $1; what bounds that risk is that every principal and every interest figure is asserted TWICE, once against its issue's own TOTAL row and once against that year's GRAND TOTAL row, and 288 assertions over 30 independent years would not all land inside $1 if the reading were loose. ONE THING THE DOCUMENT GETS WRONG AND IT IS ATTESTED, NOT TOLERATED: in FY2024 the page prints $418,704 of PRINCIPAL against `MASS WATER POOL 9*` and prints NOTHING on that issue's INTEREST row and NOTHING on its `TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST` row. The $418,704 IS in the printed `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL` for 2024 -- the fifteen principals tie to $1,973,186 EXACTLY -- and `TOTAL DEBT` for 2024 equals `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL` plus `GRAND TOTAL INTEREST` exactly, so the omission is only in the per-issue TOTAL column, which is therefore $418,704 short of the TOTAL DEBT it foots to. That is the document disagreeing with itself and it is recorded as `attested` on the FY2024 total column. WHICH FIGURE IS WRONG IS NOT ESTABLISHED and nothing on the page says. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. The page names its issues and nothing more: an issue name is not a project, and `MUNICIPAL PURPOSE` appears TWICE and `MS-HS CONSTRUCTION` TWICE with nothing printed to tell the two apart -- the `#nn` in `fund_number` is OUR ordinal, the issue's printed position down the page, and is not a number the town prints. Nor does the schedule say what the town will actually pay: the footnote states that the MWPAT amounts are to be SUBSIDIZED by equity earnings and contract assistance payments, and the amount of that subsidy is printed nowhere here. This is a FORWARD schedule of scheduled debt service as of 30 June 2017 and is a BUDGET quantity throughout; it is not an actual, and CLAUDE.md rule 1 forbids differencing it against one.
